nodes.description: AEM seawater electrolysis under industrial conditions
nodes.source_text: Lu et al. employed a NiFeBa-LDH catalyst for AEM seawater electrolysis, achieving an OER selectivity exceeding 99% in alkaline saline solutions. Under simulated industrial conditions, the electrolyzer demonstrated stable operation for 100 h at 400 mA cm⁻², 55 °C, and ambient pressure, delivering a cell voltage of 1.98 V and an energy consumption as low as 4.7 kWh Nm⁻³ H₂

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy detects characteristic Cl⁻ peak on NiFeCo(OH) material surface before reconstruction; the peak disappears after reconstruction, indicating chlorine-repellent property.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Zhou et al. employed in situ Raman spectroscopy to detect the presence of Cl⁻ on the material surface before reconstruction. Notably, the characteristic Cl⁻ peak disappeared after reconstruction, indicating that the reconstructed NiFeCo(OH) compound exhibits a chlorine-repellent property.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS investigates Cl⁻ species on electrode material surface to explore its OER selectivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similarly, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed by Qiao et al. to investigate the Cl⁻ species on the surface of electrode material, thereby exploring its OER selectivity.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy of NiMoFe/NM catalyst shows α-Ni(OH)₂ peaks disappear at 1.34 V, replaced by γ-NiOOH peaks at 476 cm⁻¹ (E_g bending) and 554 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g} stretching); peaks intensify at 1.52 V and revert to α-Ni(OH)₂ at 1.23 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Deng et al. have extensively investigated the reconstruction behavior of the NiMoFe/NM catalyst during seawater electrolysis using in situ Raman spectroscopy. At 1.34 V, the characteristic peaks of α-Ni(OH)₂ in the Raman spectrum disappear, replaced by new peaks at 476 and 554 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the E_g bending vibrations and A_{1g} stretching vibrations of NiIII-O in γ-NiOOH, respectively.
